handler: cc (Opus). Owner directive 2026-08-08: E5 stopped; arithmetic passed but the economic specification is not thereby accepted.

what_is_frozen_elsewhere_and_does_not_mo.explicit_period: 3 years, B_t = B_(t-1) + E_t × (1 − payout), RI_t = E_t − Ke × B_(t-1)
what_is_frozen_elsewhere_and_does_not_mo.note: Only the terminal changes. Every other input stays exactly as frozen, so any difference between specifications is attributable to the terminal alone.

the_question: Is the current canonical terminal too conservative to serve as a broad-index Base? A zero-growth residual-income perpetuity holds book at B3 forever, which is arithmetically identical to assuming the index pays out 100% of earnings from year 4 onward. That is internally consistent but it denies the index any reinvestment at a positive spread, and a broad equity index does reinvest.

A_zero_growth.implied_state: book frozen at B3, payout 100% of earnings, ROE = LTROE forever
A_zero_growth.role: BASELINE ONLY. Carried so the comparison has a floor, not as a candidate Base.

B_stable_growth.formula: RI_4 = (LTROE − Ke) × B3 ;  CV3 = RI_4 / (Ke − g_stable)
B_stable_growth.g_stable_provenance: Damodaran's stated cap: stable growth in a currency cannot exceed the risk-free rate in that currency, because the risk-free rate embeds long-run nominal growth expectations. The value is an observed input already inside this model, not a new number and not one chosen by looking at output.
B_stable_growth.consistency_requirement: implied stable retention b = g_stable / LTROE must lie in [0,1] and the residual payout (1−b) must be reported. This is what ties g to reinvestment rather than letting growth appear from nowhere.
B_stable_growth.finiteness_requirement: g_stable < Ke for every cell. With Ke from 0.0916 to 0.1016 and g_stable 0.0463 this holds by construction; it is asserted mechanically anyway.
B_stable_growth.why_not_the_current_payout: Carrying the explicit-period retention into perpetuity is arithmetically impossible here. SPX retention is 79.3% at LTROE 21.98%, implying g = 17.4% against a Ke near 9.7%. Any specification that lets the observed retention persist forever produces a negative denominator, and that is the honest reason the stable state must use a lower retention, not a modelling preference.

C_roe_fade.formula: ROE declines linearly from ROE_FY3 to LTROE over N years; book keeps rolling with the explicit-period payout; after the fade a zero-growth RI perpetuity at LTROE on the faded book
C_roe_fade.N_provenance: The 10-year window already present in the superseded valuation_range_v1 fade endpoint, and within the fade horizons used in the GLS literature. Not a new number and not tuned.
C_roe_fade.roe_fy3_definition: ROE_FY3 = E3 / B2, computed from the frozen explicit-period operands
C_roe_fade.book_during_fade: B_(t) = B_(t-1) + E_t × (1 − payout), with E_t = ROE_t × B_(t-1) and ROE_t on the linear fade path
C_roe_fade.direction_is_not_assumed: If ROE_FY3 exceeds LTROE the fade is downward and C sits above A; if it is below, C sits below A. The specification does not presume which.

D_yoo_exact.condition_to_admit: one common equation reproducing several public 3×3 matrices with no per-report fitted constant
D_yoo_exact.why_it_stays_out: E0 tested the only fixture held locally, the Murata 2019 grid, and refuted the linear-in-LTROE family that covers A and C's terminal structure: the grid's second LTROE step is 3.4% larger than its first at all three discount rates. One fixture can refute but cannot identify, and no second complete public matrix is held here. Admitting D would require acquiring another matrix first.

outputs_required_per_specification: terminal value share of V0 at the Base cell
current-price implied LTROE at ERP base
current-price implied ERP at LTROE base
payout route A vs B valuation impact on Base and grid mean

interpretability_test_frozen_before_resu.purpose: The owner asked whether a specification is economically interpretable. That must be decidable without looking at whether its answer is comfortable.
conditions_all_required: every cell finite and the terminal denominator strictly positive
monotonic in both axes and BULL ≥ BASE ≥ BEAR
implied stable retention, where the specification has one, inside [0,1]
terminal value share of V0 at Base strictly below 0.90 — above that the three explicit years are decoration and the model is a terminal-value calculator wearing a residual-income label
current-price implied LTROE inside the frozen alarms, 0.60 for SPX and 0.80 for NDX
current-price implied ERP inside the frozen 0.00 to 0.12 band
the terminal's assumption stateable in one sentence the owner can accept or reject without reading code
interpretability_test_frozen_before_resu.explicitly_not_a_condition: Agreement with the current market price, with any Yoo published figure, or with the other specifications. A specification that says the index is cheap or expensive is not thereby right or wrong.
interpretability_test_frozen_before_resu.selection_rule_if_several_pass: Prefer the specification whose assumption is weakest — the one that adds the least beyond what the frozen inputs already assert. Where B and C both pass, B adds a growth rate and C adds a fade path plus a horizon, so B is preferred as the smaller addition. A is never selected as Base; it is a floor.
interpretability_test_frozen_before_resu.if_none_pass: FENO_INDEX_RIM_RETIRE. Close the fair-value product, keep GLS ICC and the RIM inputs as research, and create no RIM v5 or v6.

prohibitions: no calibration to the current market price
no calibration to any Yoo published output
no g_stable, fade horizon or terminal parameter chosen after seeing a valuation
no change to the ERP or LTROE grids, which stay frozen
no editing of this file; supersede with -v2 and a new receipt
